findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Pot roast in reheating/hot holding unit on cook line had surface temperature of 94F and internal temperature of 104F-106F. Employee doing prep stated he got the foods in the unit to reheat after he arrived for work around 8a. It was 10a when temperature was checked. Mashed potatoes and BBQ pork had internal temperatures of 155F; 157F respectively. All three pans were moved to the flat grill to rapidly finish heating the foods to 165F. Smaller portions of beef and chicken gravy were already +170F.
Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. Properly reheat food to 165F/above.

**Make sure water is in the reheating/hot holding units prior to placing foods inside to reheat. Thick foods, such as roast and BBQ pork, will heat faster in smaller portions. Also, using a single pan, instead of double pan, when initially heating foods will help heat foods quicker. It is important to stir foods frequently to help heat evenly throughout the products. Staff and management need to monitor the products during heating process to ensure foods are reaching 165F within 2 hrs. After reheating is completed, then a double pan method could be used for hot holding (to help avoid burning of foods in pans) as long as the system being used is maintaining foods 135F/above during hot holding.**

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
750.140b - Pans of brown gravy, chicken gravy, and chili in walkin cooler had surface temperatures of 63F-65F and internal temperatures of 78F-83F. Manager noted the products were removed from reheat station around 12-12:30p, but time was not marked anywhere on labels of cooling foods. Manager was given option to immediately reheat for use or discard foods. All three products were already past the first two hours of cooling time frame and were voluntarily discarded. 
Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F win 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Utilize ice baths and stir foods frequently to rapidly cool foods to benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooing. The only way to know a food is properly cooling is to use a clean, calibrated stem thermometer for monitoring temperatures during cooling process. Foods can be left uncovered during cooling process as long as shelves above are clean and no raw foods (raw meats; unwashed produced) are stored above cooling foods. Label cooling foods with date and time. **Rapid chill handout provided**
